defaults.permitted_development: A loft conversion can be permitted development in Scotland where the roof enlargement stays below the existing roof height, is kept away from the roof edges, avoids front-facing enlargement and stays within the dormer-width and front-boundary limits.

rules.height_rules: The roof enlargement should not exceed the height of the existing roof.
rules.depth_rules: There is no England-style volume allowance to rely on. The practical Scottish test is whether the roof enlargement stays within the permitted size and width limits, remains back from the roof edges and avoids becoming a dominant new upper-storey form.
rules.boundary_rules: The development should be at least 10m from the boundary it fronts and more than 0.3m from any edge of the roof plane.
rules.roof_rules: Scottish permitted development for roof enlargements is much more sensitive to roof-edge clearance, dormer width and front-facing enlargement. Keeping the work off prominent front slopes and away from the roof margins is usually critical.
rules.materials_rules: Use roof materials and detailing that sit appropriately with the existing house.
